issues.legal_issue: The central government had revision jurisdiction over a pre-commencement decision concerning a rehabilitation grant when the dispute was referred to it for resolution.
material_facts: Displaced persons had received the disputed land by lease as a rehabilitation allotment before the relevant statute came into force.
A later decision rejected their request for restoration of the land, which had meanwhile been allotted to other displaced persons.
The dispute over restoration was referred to the central government, and both sides were heard before it ordered restoration.
issues.conclusion: The central government’s order fell within its revision jurisdiction because it dealt with and rectified an error concerning an earlier rehabilitation grant.
issues.legal_principle: Section 33 of the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1954 empowers the Central Government to call for records and pass an appropriate order, subject to the Act and its rules. Section 39 deems qualifying things done or actions taken before the Act commenced, including orders concerning compensation or rehabilitation grants, to have been done or taken under the Act. The court treated the referred restoration dispute as concerning such an earlier rehabilitation action, rather than viewing the matter only as review of an isolated pre-commencement order.

rule.if: rehabilitation_grant_revision_proceeding and prior_rehabilitation_allotment and restoration_dispute_referred_to_central_authority and both_sides_heard

predicates.rehabilitation_grant_revision_proceeding: The proceeding concerned review of a dispute about a grant made to rehabilitate displaced persons.
predicates.prior_rehabilitation_allotment: An authority had earlier allotted the property to displaced persons as a rehabilitation grant.
predicates.restoration_dispute_referred_to_central_: An authority referred the dispute over restoration of the earlier allotment to the central authority.
predicates.both_sides_heard: The central authority heard both sides before making its order.

issues.definition: When a rehabilitation-grant dispute about an earlier allotment is referred to the central authority and both sides are heard, the central authority has revision jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: A grant and title derived from an allotment do not survive when the underlying allotment is set aside, absent an express provision preserving them.
material_facts: Sanads were issued to the later allottees on the basis of their allotment of the land.
The allotment underlying those sanads was set aside, and the later allottees’ title depended on that allotment continuing in force.
No provision in the Act or its rules was identified as preserving the grant after the allotment was set aside; the sanad’s stated resumption condition was not fulfilled.
issues.conclusion: The sanads and the title obtained under them could not survive the setting aside of the allotment on which they were based.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 20 of the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1954 and rule 91(8), a sanad can be issued only on the basis of a valid allotment. When that allotment is set aside, the grant based on it also falls unless an express provision preserves the grant. The court approved Balwant Kaur v. Chief Settlement Commissioner (Lands), I.L.R. [1964] Punjab 36, and distinguished Partumal v. Managing Officer, Jaipur, I.L.R. 11 Rajasthan 1121.

predicates.grant_based_on_allotment: An authority issued a grant or title to a person on the basis of an allotment.
predicates.underlying_allotment_set_aside: An authority set aside the allotment on which the grant or title depended.
predicates.no_express_survival_provision: No express legal provision preserves the grant or title after the underlying allotment is set aside.

issues.definition: If a grant or title rests on an allotment that is set aside and no express provision preserves it, the grant and derived title do not survive.

issues.legal_issue: An administrative restoration order is not invalid for lack of material when the deciding authority has material on which it could find that the original lessees’ interest had not been validly terminated.
material_facts: The original allottees sought restoration of land that had been allotted to others while their lease was continuing.
A report obtained during the administrative inquiry recorded that the original allottees had personally cultivated the land.
The deciding official found that there was no justification for terminating the lease and depriving the original allottees of possession.
The appellants challenged the order on the ground that the deciding official had no material supporting it.
issues.conclusion: The challenge failed because the deciding official had material on which to find that the original allottees remained entitled to possession and that their leasehold interest had not been validly terminated.
issues.legal_principle: In an appeal under Article 136 of the Constitution, whether the central authority’s view was correct on the evidence is distinct from whether its order was legally invalid for lack of material. The court held that the authority could find on the materials before it that the leasehold interest had not been validly terminated, so the restoration order did not lack material support.

predicates.appeal_challenging_administrative_order_: A party appealed an administrative order on the ground that the deciding authority had no material to support it.
predicates.original_lessees_claimed_continuing_enti: The original lessees claimed that their leasehold interest entitled them to remain in possession.
predicates.material_supported_finding_lease_not_val: The administrative record contained material on which the deciding authority could find that the lease had not been validly terminated.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an administrative order for lack of material, but the original lessees claimed continuing entitlement and the record supported a finding that their lease was not validly terminated, the order is not invalid for lack of material.
